subject: Agent infra is easy to build. Then month 3 hits.
body_text:
A layer-by-layer breakdown of the infrastructure behind background agents.  

April 2026

**************
Ona Newsletter
**************

Ona ( https://ona.com/?utm_campaign=newsletter&utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email )

Ramp's agents write 57% of their merged PRs. Here's what they built.

Last week we mapped the background agent tool landscape ( https://background-agents.com/?utm_campaign=domino-ramp-stripe&utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email ). 103 tools across 11 layers. The most common follow-up: what does it actually take to run a platform for background agents in production?

------------------------------------------------------
Ramp's background agents write 57% of their merged PRs
------------------------------------------------------

What Ramp and Stripe built for background agents ( https://ona.com/stories/ramp-and-stripe-built-their-background-agent-infrastructure?utm_campaign=domino-ramp-stripe&utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email )

Stripe's agent platform runs on a remote dev environment they built years before GPT-3 existed. Ramp hand-rolled theirs on Modal and Cloudflare. Neither started from zero, and both have platform teams maintaining it full-time. The agent layer came last.

The blog post breaks down what they built across four layers: environments, isolation, connectivity, and automation at scale. The part worth paying attention to is what happens after the first build. Dependencies update, APIs change, integrations break. The surface area grows with every tool you connect. Most companies don't have a platform team to absorb that.

Read the full breakdown → ( https://ona.com/stories/ramp-and-stripe-built-their-background-agent-infrastructure?utm_campaign=domino-ramp-stripe&utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email )

-----------------------
Listen to the breakdown
-----------------------

We have published a lot on background agents over the past few weeks: the landscape, the Ramp and Stripe architectures, sandboxes, security. It is a lot to keep up with. So we put together a 20-minute audio walkthrough that covers the key points.

Your agents are stuck on your laptop. Here's what Stripe built instead.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

24 min

00:00 | 24:46

------------------------------------------------
We're building a self-driving codebase in public
------------------------------------------------

Starting next week, we're building a fully functioning, open-source app from scratch, entirely on Ona. No line of code written by a human. Background agents planning the architecture, writing code, opening PRs, running CI, fixing what breaks. No demo repo. No curated highlights. The full build, public, from commit zero.

We'll run live sessions as we go, document every decision and failure, and share regular updates.

We're also giving away 20x $1,000 in credits for teams and engineers that want to build alongside us. Your codebase or idea, with our support on architecture and use cases.

Apply for the self-driving codebase project → ( https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdNYonXUK0gOwy2NpbqiWOgoyHIyHkFJMy0a6dT3tXJ11tupg/viewform?utm_campaign=domino-ramp-stripe&utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email )

----------------
Landscape update
----------------

The background agent landscape keeps growing. Since launch we have added 15 tools across security, sandboxes, orchestration, review, and agents. Notable additions: Cursor Cloud, Vercel Agent, Warp, Northflank, Namespace, nono, and Agent Auth Protocol. If we missed your tool or miscategorized it, let us know.

Explore the landscape → ( https://background-agents.com/landscape?utm_campaign=domino-ramp-stripe&utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email )

--------------------------------------------
Background Agents Virtual Summit (Early May)
--------------------------------------------

Last week we mentioned we were working on a virtual summit. It is taking shape. Three tracks: scaling agent infrastructure, security and governance, and how engineering orgs actually change when agents produce a significant share of code. Every session is grounded in real architecture and real outcomes from industry leaders.

We'd love to have you join. If you are running background agents or actively building toward it and want to share what you have learned, please reach out with a simple reply.

Talk soon,

Lou
Field CTO, Ona
